intro.page_title: Roberto Vallado | Full-Stack .NET Developer | Security & Infrastructure
intro.tagline: Full-stack .NET developer who builds things that are hard to break — and knows how to prove it.
intro.p0: I'm Roberto, a full-stack developer based in Québec with five years of production experience in C# / .NET and Angular. My foundation is shipping software that works: features, APIs, databases, deployment pipelines, the full delivery chain. What I bring on top of that is an understanding of the layers most developers treat as someone else's problem — security and infrastructure.
intro.p1: I actively hunt real-world vulnerabilities on Bugcrowd. Not because I want to pivot into security, but because nothing sharpens your instincts as a developer like understanding how systems get broken. It changes how you design an API endpoint, how you think about authentication flows, how you read a pull request. At SSM Innovation Centre I built an SBOM pipeline to proactively catch vulnerable dependencies — security thinking applied directly into the delivery process.
intro.p2: On the infrastructure side, I've owned CI/CD pipelines, Docker deployments, and Terraform configurations in a lean team with no dedicated DevOps specialists. I'm currently working towards CompTIA Network+ — not to become a network engineer, but because understanding how packets move, how DNS resolves, and how TLS handshakes work closes the gap between writing code and understanding what can go wrong underneath it.
intro.p3: At SSM Innovation Centre I grew from a co-op developer to team lead: driving architecture decisions, mentoring four developers, and taking ownership of QA and DevOps responsibilities alongside regular feature delivery. I've also taught Web Applications and Business Applications Development at Sault College, which means I know how to explain complex technical decisions clearly and bring junior developers along.
intro.p4: I recently completed an AEC in Secure Application Development at Cégep Limoilou, adding formal cybersecurity foundations on top of my hands-on bug bounty research and daily development work. The combination is deliberate: I want to be the kind of developer who makes a team more resilient just by being on it.
intro.p5: If you're looking for a .NET developer who brings security awareness and infrastructure depth as a day-to-day reality — not as side interests — I'd like to talk. I'm looking for a role where quality and security are built in, not bolted on.
